title: SCE scenario set (wire schema v1)
description: Examples of what a specification says a machine does, each anchored to a sentence of the specification and written in the owner's words: which events are sent in, how much time passes, and what must be observed. A file beside the specification, written by its owner or proposed by an AI client for the owner to confirm, read by `sce-codegen scenarios`; never emitted by SCE. It carries the interface the examples are written against (a proposal the owner accepts with them), because a specification rarely names the events, payload fields and outputs an example has to mention. A scenario that cannot run says why instead of being dropped: `awaiting-decision` is a question the specification leaves open put as an example, `blocked` waits on a fact nobody has decided. SCE does not run a scenario here and does not say a design passes; this file is what an engine's observations are judged against. Authoritative reader is sce-build/src/scenario_set.rs. The stability status of this surface lives in this header alone — see SCE_WIRE_CONTRACTS.md.

name.description: A name the owner uses: an event, a condition, a data item, a payload field. Any text with no space at either end.

id.description: An identifier other entries refer to.

fieldType.description: What a payload field holds: `integer` (a whole number), `number` (any number), `text` or `boolean`.

payloadDecl.description: The fields an event carries and the type of each.

scalar.description: A value a payload field or a data item holds in an example.

payloadValue.description: Values for the fields of an event, by field name.

route.description: How an output leaves the machine: the Event I/O Processor type and the target it is sent to. An output with no route is one whose route nobody has decided, and a run cannot observe it.

interface.description: The names the examples are written against. A proposal: it becomes the machine's interface when the owner accepts it with the examples.

why.description: Why these names, and which of them the specification gives and which are proposed.

conditions.description: States the specification itself names. An example may say a machine is in one of them; a state the specification does not name is not something an example can mention.

data.description: Data items the specification itself names.

world.description: Facts an example relies on that the specification does not give, such as a price list. The values are placeholders for a decision, not facts, and `source` says where the real ones come from, or `undecided`.

expectOutbound.description: An event the machine sent to something outside itself. Without `payload` the payload is not checked.

expect.description: What must be observed after the step. `outbound` is every event sent outward during the step, in order, and `[]` means none: an example is as much about what does not happen. Anything left out is not checked.

step.description: One thing that happens, then what is observed. A step with neither `send` nor `advance_ms` observes without acting: step 0 of a scenario is judged on the initial configuration.

advance_ms.description: Virtual time that passes, in milliseconds. Never wall-clock time.

decision.description: The question a scenario waits on. `alternatives` names the scenarios of which exactly one is kept once the owner has answered.

quote.description: The sentence of the specification this example is about, word for word. `sce-codegen scenarios --specification` refuses one that is not there.

requirements.description: Ids of the requirement list this example is evidence for. A scenario that passes for a requirement met by something not happening is what settles a `needs-scenario` outcome.

blocked_by.description: What a blocked scenario waits on.

assumes.description: Facts the example takes as given that the specification does not state, such as the condition the machine starts in.

bound.description: How far a run went when the sentence claims something no run can show, such as 'indefinitely'. A result says it was bounded.

record.description: Names this file as a scenario set, so a file of another kind is refused rather than half read.

v.description: The wire version of this record. A file of another version is refused.

specification.description: The specification the quotes are taken from, as the requirement list names it.

origin.description: Who wrote the examples. A declaration only: SCE cannot verify it and repeats it in every result. `ai-proposed` examples are a reading of the specification until the owner confirms them.
